OGE (OGE) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Motley Fool Transcribing

DATE
Wednesday, April 29, 2026 at 9 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer — R. Trauschke
Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer — Charles Walworth
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email

TAKEAWAYS
Consolidated Earnings
-- $0.24 per diluted share, with consolidated net income of approximately $50 million.
Electric Segment Earnings
-- Net income of $58 million or $0.28 per diluted share, down from $71 million or $0.35 per share due to milder weather and O&M timing.
Guidance Affirmed
-- Management reiterated 2026 consolidated earnings guidance of $2.43 per share, within a $2.38 to $2.48 range, conditional on normal weather.
Customer Growth
-- Growth reported "just under 1%," with weather-normalized load described as stable, despite temporary large customer outages offset by sectoral strength.
Google Data Center Contracts
-- Planned long-term special contracts with
Google
(NASDAQ: GOOGL) will be filed imminently; Google pays all connection costs and minimum charges, with "expected load and ramp rate is consistent with our 2026 IRP."
Solar Capacity Contracts
-- Two under-construction solar facilities will provide 600 megawatts of nameplate capacity through capacity purchase agreements to serve Google's load.
Generation Investments
-- Recently commissioned 98-megawatt Tinker plant; 450 megawatts at Horseshoe Lake expected online in Q4, with ground broken for two additional 450-megawatt units and a 300-megawatt Frontier Energy storage project advancing.
Planned Capacity Additions
-- Combined, 1.7 gigawatts of new capacity—including solar agreements—are flagged as strengthening system readiness and supporting future growth.
Regulatory Initiatives
-- Stand-alone large load tariff to be filed with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission by July 1; rate review filing expected later in the year with targeted effective new rates in 2027.
Preapprovals and Approvals
-- Anticipated August preapproval for Frontier Energy Storage, rolling project preapproval filings during the year, and October target for finalizing SPP transmission construction notices.
Financing Actions
-- April debt issuance meets 2026 financing needs; current flexibility to exercise 4.6 million shares in forward equity agreements through May 2027.
Credit Outlook
-- Moody's revised outlooks for OGE Energy and OG&E to stable from negative and affirmed all ratings, lowering the parent downgrade FFO to debt threshold to 17%.
Short-term Load Growth Guidance
-- 4%-6% range reiterated for the year, with no updated long-term growth guidance yet provided.
Capital Plan Visibility
-- Future generation and transmission projects—including RFP outcomes—will be integrated into the capital plan as approvals occur, with detailed financial implications communicated at that time.
Customer Protections
-- Contracts with data center customers include multiyear commitments, minimum charges, exit provisions, and strong credit backing to mitigate risks and protect existing customers.
SUMMARY
Management provided operational and regulatory clarity, citing imminent filings of special contracts with Google and the upcoming introduction of a large load tariff to address growing data center demand. The company reported recent and planned major capacity additions, emphasizing that these investments align with the current integrated resource plan and are not incremental to previously disclosed load growth projections. There is ongoing preparation for increased project approval activity through the year, including battery storage and SPP transmission projects. Steps taken in April, including a debt issuance, have fulfilled present financing requirements, while Moody's revision to a stable credit outlook reflects progress on regulatory, financing, and capital structure fronts. No new guidance has been issued for long-term earnings or load growth beyond the base range, pending project approvals and capital plan integration.
The described structure of Google agreements allows the spreading of fixed costs to reduce pressure on existing customer rates.
Charles Walworth stated, "this announcement is consistent with what's in our IRP," confirming that Google's load and associated solar contracts were accounted for in the established plan.
Management continues to prioritize ownership and operation of generation assets, citing asset performance in severe weather as a driving rationale.
The large load tariff filing and related legislative initiatives are designed to protect both new and existing customers by formalizing terms, thresholds, and capital commitments.
Bids for new generation resources from the RFP remain in process; project timing and approval windows are communicated as contingent on ongoing regulatory milestones.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
IRP (Integrated Resource Plan)
: A utility’s comprehensive plan outlining forecasted demand and the generation resources required to reliably and cost-effectively serve projected load over a defined planning horizon.
SPP (Southwest Power Pool)
: The regional transmission organization responsible for grid reliability and wholesale electricity markets in parts of Oklahoma, Arkansas, and neighboring states.
CPA (Capacity Purchase Agreement)
: A contract under which a utility secures availability of a specified quantity of generation capacity from another party to meet its system needs.
O&M (Operations and Maintenance)
: Costs associated with day-to-day operation and routine maintenance of utility assets.
FFO (Funds From Operations)
: A cash flow metric reflecting earnings plus non-cash items, used in credit analysis to assess financial flexibility.

I couldn't be more proud to work alongside my outstanding colleagues. Their commitment to our purpose is evident every day and continues to drive excellence. and our commitment to making Oklahoma and Arkansas better places to live, work and play drives us to our North Star of delivering reliable electricity at low cost.
